title: King and pawn against king: name the deciding condition
outcomes: Names the controlling condition of a K+P v K result and tests it by changing only that fact
Plays out a won position and a drawn one against the tablebase-backed opponent

steps.text: After **King and pawn against king: predict the family** you can say what the result is. Now say why. Often one fact decides a result: change it and the result flips. Look for it: who is to move; which king reaches the squares in front of the pawn; the edge file and corner; a pawn pushed too early. Name it, then test it. First, hold a draw.

steps.caption: Black to move. Only Kd3 holds the draw here; the other king moves lose.

line.say: Black's king steps to d3, beside the pawn, and attacks it.
White's king steps to b2 to defend the pawn.

claims.statement: Black can hold the draw from the start position.

steps.text: Naming a condition is a claim you can test: change only that fact and predict again. If the result does not change, that fact was not what decided this position; try another. Compare the next three positions, then write one sentence for each result you play. These are claims about positions, not general laws.

steps.title: Which fact decides?
steps.prompt: In the first position White to move wins. Predict the second, where only the move changes, and the third, where the pawn is one square further.
For each of the last three positions, name the controlling condition: the one fact that, if changed, would flip the result. Then test it in your head.
